params.requirement: Answers a fixed set of typed choices about one short spoken or typed request: which topic it belongs to, if any, and which block would show it best. It needs a fast, cheap decider that returns a calibrated probability per answer, never generated text. It runs on every turn while the person waits for the screen, so an answer must come back within a few hundred milliseconds and cost next to nothing.

model.description: The decider's model id (`PRESENTER_DECIDE_MODEL`). Empty as shipped: a presenter without a decider shows nothing, and every turn's journal row says `no_selector`. Changed at runtime by the model registry's overlay.

api_key.description: The decider's key (`PRESENTER_DECIDE_API_KEY`), or a `credential_grant_id` in its place.

base_url.description: The decider's endpoint (`PRESENTER_DECIDE_BASE_URL`); the template README names an example.

base_url_allow.description: The origins (`scheme://host[:port]`) a push of the model registry may move `base_url` to. Empty as shipped -- the template names no provider -- so a push that carries an endpoint is refused (`model_refused`) until the set that installs the presenter lists the endpoint of its decisions rows here (`override_params`). Immutable at run time, like every allow list of the llm cell.

description.purpose: The decider: ONE call per turn over a fixed set of questions (the topic, and per topic the lead and the second block), answered as one `decision` with a confidence per answer.
description.use_when: Always, as part of the presenter; born with `provider: decisions`, which never changes after spawn.
description.not_in_scope: It sees the turn's text and the descriptions of topics and candidates -- never fetched data and never memory. No tools, no chat model: the registry never hands this cell one.
